Jibin: Flight-control software verification. Basically proving the code does what it should, every time. Lots of test rigs. If a rig does something strange, they come to me.
Hodan: See, that's the same as me. If something's gone wrong in the department, they come to me. I do the final accuracy checks, I run the rota, and I keep my own spreadsheet of every near-miss, because if you don't track it, it didn't happen, you know.
Jibin: Yes, exactly. Data. People don't like it, but data is data.
Hodan: People hate it. I've got juniors who think I'm scary. I'm not scary, I just don't want anyone getting the wrong drug.
Jibin: To be honest, I have the same reputation. Difficult but usually right.
Hodan: Ha! Difficult but usually right, I'm having that. What band would you be in, if you was NHS?
Jibin: Er, it doesn't map exactly. I'm senior, I want principal. I think I'm overdue, actually. Two people went ahead of me last round and I'm still not sure why.
Hodan: You've got to make noise, though. I pushed through a regrading last year. I just kept going to my manager with evidence until she couldn't say no. Now I want Band 6 lead technician in two years, medicines optimisation.
Jibin: Yes, but sometimes the evidence is there and still. Sorry, what's medicines optimisation exactly?
Hodan: Kind of making sure patients are on the right meds, reviewing, less firefighting. Better hours, better money.
Jibin: Better hours is important. You have a son, I saw the photo?
Hodan: Idris, he's eight. Just me and him, my mum helps. What do you do for fun, apart from spreadsheets?
Jibin: Badminton, Thursdays. Parkrun sometimes, because my GP mentioned my cholesterol.
Hodan: Do you track your times?
Jibin: Of course.
Hodan: Good. I do weights three mornings a week, I log every lift. I did mine at six this morning.
Jibin: Six. Okay, that's dedicated. I struggle with eight on a Saturday.
Hodan: You just get used to it. And badminton, are you competitive?
Jibin: Very. There's one man in our group who never calls his own faults. Every week.
Hodan: Oh my days, I'd be fuming. Sorry, go on.
Jibin: No, it's fine. I argue the line calls. Probably too much, my friends say.
Hodan: Nah, if he's wrong, he's wrong, innit—
calls.C0147:
Hodan: Hi! Last one, yeah? I'm Hodan, Wembley.
Neil: Hello. Neil. Basingstoke. Yeah, I think this is the last one.
Hodan: Thank God, my brain's going. How've you found it?
Neil: Fine, actually. Everyone's been very nice. It's more talking than I'd normally do in an evening, mind.
Hodan: Ha! Not me, I could go all night. So what do you do? I had you down as a manager or a GP or something.
Neil: Er, no. Civil engineer. Water company. Pumping stations and sewers, north Hampshire. My wife's at a GP surgery, though, she's the practice manager. Part-time.
Hodan: Oh, okay, so she knows the NHS chaos. I'm a pharmacy technician, senior, at a hospital in North West London. Aseptic and dispensary.
Neil: She'd get on with you, I think. She's always on about prescriptions going missing between the surgery and the chemist.
Hodan: Honestly, that's half my life. Somebody upstream doesn't do their job properly and then it lands on us and we look like the problem. I keep a spreadsheet of every near-miss in the department, so when anyone tries it, I've got it in black and white.
Neil: That's sensible. I'm the same with the pump stations. If you've written it down, nobody can argue with you.
Hodan: Exactly! See, people think it's petty but it's not.
Neil: No.
Hodan: What do you do outside work, then? You seem like a garden person.
Neil: Yeah, a bit. Tomatoes, runner beans. Walk the dog. Watch Reading lose.
Hodan: Reading! Oh, that's rough. I'm Arsenal, well, my brothers are, I just watch with them for the arguing.
Neil: Arsenal's a bit of a different experience, I'd imagine.
Hodan: Ha, yeah, we complain when we draw. Did you have a bad commute today? The Jubilee line was down again, I was stood on a platform for twenty minutes and then I got a parking ticket last week, which I'm appealing, by the way, on principle, because the sign was literally behind a tree.
Neil: Behind a tree?
Hodan: Behind a tree! I've got photos.
Neil: You'll win that, then. Er, mine's the A33. Roadworks. Nothing exciting.
Hodan: Do you have kids? Sorry, I always ask everyone that.
Neil: That's all right. Two, both grown up. Daughter's in Southampton, son's at Nottingham. Your lad's eight, isn't he? I saw the photo.
Hodan: Yeah, Idris. He's at the age where he asks a question every five seconds. My mum does his pickups when I'm on lates, I don't know what I'd do without her. She's getting older, though, and I kind of rely on her a lot. Anyway.
Neil: Yeah. Mine's seventy-nine, on her own in Reading. You don't really notice it happening, and then you do.
Hodan: Yeah. That's it, you know.
Neil: Make the most of her, I suppose. That's about all you can do.
Hodan: Erm, yeah. Fair. Sorry, that got deep for a last call.
Neil: No, that's fine. Better than the weather.
Hodan: Ha! Okay, quick one, Cornwall or abroad?
Neil: Cornwall. Padstow. Every year.
Hodan: Every year? You don't get bored?
Neil: No. That's sort of the point.
calls.C0148:
Kerry: Hiya. Can you hear me?
Jibin: Yes, fine. I'm Jibin, near Bristol. Bradley Stoke.
Kerry: Kerry. Bridgwater. So we're practically neighbours.
Jibin: Practically. Forty minutes on the M5 if the Filton junction is not a disaster. Which it always is.
Kerry: Ha. Yeah. What do you do, then? I'm guessing something with computers.
Jibin: Embedded software. Aerospace. Flight-control verification, basically.
Kerry: Right. Sounds like you'd be picky.
Jibin: Er, it's a job where you have to be picky, to be honest. If I'm not picky, that's a problem.
Kerry: Fair enough. I'm a painter and decorator, so I'm picky about different stuff.
Jibin: Okay. Actually, maybe you can tell me something. We're in a new-build, four years, and the developer never fixed the snagging. There are cracks where the walls meet the ceiling, in almost every room. They said it's normal.
Kerry: It is normal, to be fair. New-builds settle, the plaster dries out, you get hairline cracks along the joins. Everyone gets them.
Jibin: But four years? It should have finished settling, surely.
Kerry: Mostly, yeah. You rake them out, flexible filler, or decorator's caulk on the corners, sand it, then paint. Don't just slap emulsion over, it'll come back.
Jibin: Caulk. Not normal filler?
Kerry: On the corner joins, caulk, because it moves. Flat bits of wall, filler. That's what I'd do anyway, I've done about a hundred of them.
Jibin: Okay. That makes sense, actually. I'd assumed it was structural.
Kerry: If you can get a coin in it, ring someone. If it's a hairline, it's not.
Jibin: Good test. Cheers.
Kerry: No worries. Do you do your own decorating, then?
Jibin: Er, I did one room. My wife says never again. I'm better with the thermostat. I have a smart system, every room separate, it saves quite a lot on the bills.
Kerry: I rent, so I just put a jumper on.
Jibin: Fair enough. Bridgwater, is that near Taunton? I go to the cricket at Taunton sometimes.
Kerry: Yeah, twenty minutes. My son's dad lives there. Jayden goes every other weekend.
Jibin: Okay. Does he play cricket? Your son?
Kerry: No, football. Sunday league. I'm on the touchline every week shouting.
Jibin: My son is twelve, he does nothing outside except complain. He wants a gaming PC.
Kerry: Oh, Jayden's on about one of them. They're a fortune, aren't they.
Jibin: They are if you buy the prebuilt ones. You're paying for the lights and the brand. If you choose the parts yourself, much better value. Graphics card is where you spend, the rest you can be sensible.
Kerry: See, I wouldn't have a clue what any of that means.
Jibin: I can tell you what to look for, if you like. Just quickly.
Kerry: Go on then. Jayden'll think I'm a genius.
Jibin: Basically, don't let him choose the—

C0146.line_text: Idris, he's eight. Just me and him, my mum helps. What do you do for fun, apart from spreadsheets?
C0146.what: A young boy in pyjamas walks across the living room behind Hodan, passing in front of the grey sofa and the folded laundry pile, picks up a book from the shelf and walks back out of frame. Hodan doesn't turn around and keeps talking.
